newsitem.title: USA: US Labor Dept economist sees no higher price trend.
newsitem.headline: US Labor Dept economist sees no higher price trend.

text.p: A slight acceleration in consumer price rises in the past three months does not suggest a trend toward accelerating inflation, a Labor Department economist said Thursday.

Steve Grandits, an economist at the department's Bureau of Labor Statistics, noted the compounded rise in the Consumer Price Index for the Sept-Nov period was 3.3 percent, slightly higher than the rate of increase in the past two years. The increase in the core rate, which excludes food and energy, has been fairly stable, he said.
"I'm not sure I see a trend that concerns me in either one of those numbers," Grandits said in an interview on Reuters Financial Television.

Grandits said the 0.3 percent rise in the November CPI was largely driven by a 1.2 percent spurt in energy prices, which he blamed mostly on fuel oil price hikes after unseasonably cold weather during the month. But he noted that crude oil prices have already begun to soften this month.
"Certainly, if energy continues (to rise), inflation will stay at that slightly higher rate, but I don't know that I see anything that concerns me in particular," he said.
Helping to moderate the rise in overall prices last month was a slowing of food price increases in November to 0.3 percent after a 0.6 percent October rise.
"It suggests to me that perhaps some of the concerns over the harvest this year ... haven't really come to pass and we've had good harvests and good crops this year," said Grandits.
